question: What must an applicant provide to evidence a common-law union?

claims.text: An applicant with common-law marital status must submit a Statutory Declaration of Common-Law Union (IMM 5409) and evidence of continuous cohabitation for at least 12 months.
claims.quote: The applicant must submit a Statutory Declaration of Common-Law Union form [[IMM 5409 (PDF, 636.51 KB)](https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/ircc/migration/ircc/english/pdf/kits/forms/imm5409e.pdf)] and evidence of cohabitation for a period of at least 12 continuous months.

claims.text: Acceptable evidence of cohabitation includes joint bank account statements, leases, and utility bills.

basis: The applicant submitted a 2-page Statutory Declaration of Common-Law Union (IMM 5409) document for Express Entry completeness review.
The document was reviewed against IRCC completeness requirements for common-law union documentation, including solemnization, 12-month continuous cohabitation evidence, and financial interdependence.
prose: When marital status is listed as common-law, Express Entry applicants must submit a Statutory Declaration of Common-Law Union (IMM 5409) along with proof of continuous cohabitation for at least 12 months, such as joint bank statements, joint leases, or utility bills.
